On a leadership role I was recruiting for, we stopped and took a second look at the bachelor's degree requirement.

What we found: it was screening out candidates who had the actual skills the role needed.

The takeaway: skills-based hiring isn't just a buzzword. Sometimes the requirement that's been on a job description for years is the exact thing keeping your best candidate from applying.

Hiring managers: when did you last ask whether every requirement on your job post is truly required?

'Culture fit' is often just a euphemism for 'reminds me of me.'

When hiring managers can't articulate specific behaviors or values they're screening for, culture fit becomes a way to justify hiring people who feel familiar. The fix isn't abandoning culture as a hiring criterion, it's defining it specifically enough that it can't be used as a shortcut for sameness.

How does your organization actually define culture fit, in specific behavioral terms?

🎯 A moment from this week:

I've noticed candidates treat recorded video interviews more casually than live ones.

It's an easy habit to fall into. But that recording often gets shared with the entire hiring team afterward.

The takeaway: treat a recorded interview exactly like an in-person one. Find a quiet space, dress the same way you would face to face, and remember more than one person may watch it later.

Job seekers: if you have a recorded interview coming up, set it up like the real meeting it is.

#InterviewTips #JobSearch #NeoHRUS

Is this the right offer, and am I set up to make an impact from day one?

Most people accept the first offer out of relief after a long search. Impact builds the muscle to pause, research, and ask, calmly and specifically, then evaluate the whole offer, not just base salary. The phase ends when you start the new role positioned to deliver.

Your goal for this phase: Have a researched target range, a rehearsed ask, and a full-offer evaluation before accepting, then a first-90-days plan for a strong start.

Can you say your ask out loud, exactly how you'd say it to them?

Watch out for: Accepting the first offer out of fear the ask will cost you the job. A reasonable, well-researched ask essentially never rescinds an offer.

You're ready to move on when: You've said your ask out loud before the real conversation, evaluated the full offer, and drafted your first-90-days plan.

In the Spine of Your Job Search playbook: Module 6: Negotiate, Don't Settle
